title: findings_register.v2
description: The CAPA register, version 2: one row per finding in the proof journal (docs/POC_JOURNAL.md), kept at docs/FINDINGS_REGISTER.json. The journal is the immutable record of each finding; the register is its living status: risk ranking, deadline, closure, and verification. Severity rubric: critical = an exploitable security exposure or a control that admits what it must refuse (fix within 7 days); high = a control that silently does not run or checks nothing, or a governance gap that removes a guardrail (30 days); medium = a defect or missing proof with a working control around it (90 days); low = maintainability or reuse (180 days). A row's due date is at most its found date plus its severity's days, checked by tests/journal/register.py, which also fails an overdue open finding on the daily run, computes the control-effectiveness metrics, and reports production readiness: false while any critical or high finding in the security or governance category is open. Version 2 names the register's agent (KAN-60) and adds what the CAPA graph needs (06_AgentZone/10_CAPA_Graph_and_Risk_Weighted_Learning.md §2, §4): a registry of components with their dependencies, and on every finding machine-readable references to the rules it breaks, the components it affects, its defect fingerprints, matching anti-patterns, and the earlier findings it recurs. tests/journal/register.py resolves every reference against its source (rule catalogs, playbook headings, the anti-pattern catalog, this registry) and rejects one that does not resolve; nothing is guessed. findings_register.v1 stays accepted for the deprecation window stated in that check.

agent.description: The agent whose journal and register this is (KAN-60): builder for the factory platform's register, pentest later. Each agent reads only its own register, so finding IDs are unambiguous within it.

components.description: Every component a finding can affect. depends_on edges point from the dependent to its dependency; the graph's centrality is computed on them.

controls.description: The gate's control classes, each proven or not: shown to fail on the defect it guards against. The share proven is a control-effectiveness metric.

detected_by.description: control: a check, scanner, or test reported it; person: someone looking found it. Set by hand and not yet verified against evidence: the share recorded as found by controls is reported as an attribution, not as verified detection effectiveness.

status.description: fixed: the correction and preventive action are in place; proven: a designed-to-fail case shows the control catches the defect.

verification.description: Where the proof is: runs, commits, pull requests, reports.

residual.description: What a closed finding still leaves open, stated rather than implied.

refs.description: Machine-readable references for the CAPA graph. Each is resolved by tests/journal/register.py.

rule_ids.description: The rules the finding breaks: a catalog ID (ARCH-NNN in architecture_rules.v1, SEC-NNN in 07_Security_In_Depth.md, GOV-NNN in governance_baseline.v1), or PATH#HEADING: a playbook Markdown file and the exact text of one of its headings, without a leading emoji number.

fingerprints.description: Stable slugs of the defect patterns. Two findings with a shared fingerprint and a shared rule are the same pattern.

recurs.description: Earlier findings this one recurs: closed before this one was found, sharing a fingerprint and a rule.

ticket.description: The finding's ticket key (KAN-60 slice 4). Optional in v2; the check that requires it on open rows comes with that slice.

name.description: How the journal names it: a repository name, or a cloud project or account as described.
